messages:
cheng: heads-up — seeing intermittent late writeback on ephemerals in us-west2 that's stalling GPU attach jobs.
alex: noticed same, GPU queue rising ~6% last 10m, provisioning latency +120s.
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme-writeback-lag detected on cluster us-west2-ephemeral at 3123456792
maria: logs? paste output from iostat /proc/diskstats?
cheng: here's quick snap:
```text
Device       wt(sec)  await  r/s  w/s  avgqu-sz
nvme0n1      12.3     350   1.2  210  5.4
```
alex: w/s high + avgqu large. Could be late writeback queueing due to background scrub?
maria: scrub windows were bumped yesterday; janitor overlap?
dave: we rolled janitor cadence to 3:00->4:30, GPU drain starts 3:15 — overlap possible.
cheng: hypothesis: janitor deep-scrub touching large tmpfiles causing dirty pages, writeback holds, nvme IO saturates, evict backpressure -> GPU attach blocked.
alex: mitigation: throttle janitor, or bump janitor to lower priority. Anyone got quick fix?
maria: trying throttle now: `kubectl patch cronjob janitor --patch '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid"}}'` not ideal but quick.
ops-bot: ACTION_STARTED: patch applied 3123456798 by maria
alex: after throttle, I see attach queue drop to baseline in ~45s.
dave: still seeing some writeback tails — maybe kernel flush params? try `echo 10 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_expire_centisecs` on canary host
cheng: doing that on 3 canaries
cheng: canaries show writeback latency down to 2.1s, GPU attach resumes normal
maria: opened infra ticket -> INFRA-1129, assigning eng-infra
alex: long-term: need janitor QoS, or route janitor to lower-cost pool to avoid interfering with hot GPU pools. cost tradeoffs? if we move janitor off hot nodes increased egress/provisioning cost.
dave: cost vs SLA: prefer small dedicated janitor fleet for ephemerals.
cheng: recording postmortem notes in #postmortems later. for now monitoring alert thresholds lowered, and janitor cadence reverted to safe window.
maria: :thumbsup:
cheng: thanks all. closing thread.
